name: a worn footpath of packed earth between shacks, lighter than the surrounding dirt, with faint wheel ruts and footprints, its edges feathering softly into the dirt with no outline, laid as a path network with crossings and dead ends

surfaces.part: packed earth ground tile with lighter footpath, ruts and footprints

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256x192 flat ground texture. Every row has width 256, with no silhouette, no front face, no edge line and no eave shadow. The column scan shows only repeating dirt-speckle bands, with no vertical face. This is flat terrain seen from above, which is correct for a ground tile of kind terrain, so the object has no standing structure to measure.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a mottled brown dirt built from only 7 colours, which read as about 3 visible tones per tile: a mid brown, a darker patch tone and a light speckle. That matches the grass reference on visible tones (3 vs 3) and is far below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no big flat fills. There is no outline, which suits a feathered edge. The ramp is shallow next to Beodeul's 5-6 steps per material, and the grass reference gets much more variation from clumps, tufts and dozens of greens. The texture is a busy, repetitive noise with visible tiling and little structure. There are no per-clump highlights, no grain direction, and nothing that reads as a lighter packed-earth path with ruts or footprints against darker surrounding dirt. The path and the surrounding dirt look like one ramp, so the piece looks like a flat noise fill rather than a crafted ground. Doubt resolves to fail.

surfaces.part: packed earth ground tile (path network over dirt)

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256x192 ground texture of brown dirt with a lighter packed-earth path, ruts and speckles. Every row is 256 px wide, so there is no silhouette, no front face, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse. This is flat top-down terrain, which is what the terrain kind expects. The column scans show only mottled dirt variation, with no structural edges.

styleAnswer.evidence: On the primary facts the candidate matches the grass reference: 3 visible tones per tile, 2% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges. It has no outline, which suits a feathered path edge, and no large flat fills. It falls short in three ways. First, the whole patch uses only 7 distinct colours, so the dirt and the lighter path each get about 3 tones, against the roughly 5-6 steps Beodeul uses per material. Second, the texture is a uniform salt-and-pepper speckle with scattered dark blobs. It lacks the clustered tufts and per-feature shading of the grass reference, and the paving reference is far richer at 7 tones. Third, the lighter path, ruts, footprints and crossings are barely legible, and only a faint lighter zone shows on the right. The repeating noise pattern reads as a tiled dirt field, not a worn path network. Because the ramps are shallow and the path structure is weak, it would look thinner than the references, so it fails.

surfaces.part: packed earth ground tile with lighter footpath network, ruts and footprints

answer.evidence: The image is a full-bleed 256x192 terrain tile of dirt texture. The silhouette is 256 wide on every row, with no outline, no standing body, no front face and no edge line. This is flat ground seen from above, which is correct for terrain. The column scan shows repeating patches of lighter and darker dirt (L about 81 to 115) with no front-edge line or eave shadow. The lighter footpath areas, ruts and footprints are texture variations on the flat ground.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a ground patch, so the grass and paving references are the right kind. It shows 3 visible tones per tile, the same as the grass reference (3) and below the paving (7). Near-flat coverage is 2% against 0% for both references, so there are no real flat fills. The brown soil is dense with speckles, grit clusters and darker blotches. I count about 4 lightness steps across 7 total colours, a bit shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 but comparable to the grass tile. No outline is drawn, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so there is no sticker look. The edges and noise read as soft soil grain. A lighter footpath with ruts and feathered edges is faintly visible at best, but this review judges only shading craft, and on that the candidate sits at the grass reference level. It is slightly less rich than the paving and a little repetitive, but it is not shallow.
